p.seg: *Yáo Diǎn*
Long ago, the Emperor Yáo
was intelligent and discerning, possessing literary talent and profound thought.
His radiance filled the world.
When he intended to abdicate his throne,
he yielded it to Yú Shùn.
Thus, the *Yáo Diǎn* was composed.
It is said that,
Investigating the ancient records:
Emperor Yáo was named Fàngxūn.
He was cultured, thoughtful, and content;
Truly respectful, compliant, and yielding;
His radiance covered the four quarters of the world,
Reaching to those above and below.
He was able to illuminate outstanding virtue
in order to be close to the nine branches of his clan;
Once the nine branches of his clan were harmonious,
he distinguished
and clarified the hundred surnames,
and harmonized the myriad states.
The black-haired people consequently changed and became full and prosperous,
at that time living in harmony.
Then he commanded Xī Hé,
to respectfully comply with the vast heaven;
To calculate and observe the sun, moon, and stars,
and respectfully instruct the people on the seasons.
He separately ordered Xī Zhòng,
to reside in Yúyí,
called Yánggǔ.
Respectfully welcoming the rising sun,
to regulate the work of the east.
When the sun is at its zenith and the star is Niǎo (Bird),
to accurately mark the middle of spring.
At that time, the people disperse;
birds and beasts breed.
He again ordered Xī Shū,
to reside in the south, called Dàjiāo.
To regulate the changes of the south.
To respectfully present (offerings).
When the days are long and the star is Huǒ (Fire),
to accurately mark the middle of summer.
At that time, the people are settled;
the birds and beasts undergo sparse changes.
He separately ordered Hé Zhòng to reside in the west,
called Màigǔ.
Respectfully escorting the setting sun,
to regulate the completion of the west.
When the night is at its midpoint and the star is Xū (Emptiness),
to accurately mark the middle of autumn.
At that time, the people are at peace;
the birds and beasts grow new hair.
He again ordered Hé Shū,
to reside in the north,
called Yōudū.
The sun's shadow is at its shortest in Shuòyì.
The days are short, and the stars are at Mǎo,
to determine the middle of winter.
Its people live in warm dwellings;
birds and beasts have thick fur.
The Emperor said:
"Ah! You, Xī and Hé,
calculate three hundred sixty and six days,
using an intercalary month
to determine the four seasons and complete the year.
Faithfully regulate the officials,
and all their achievements will be splendid."
The Emperor said:
"Who can I consult about the times, so as to promote them?"
Fàngqí said:
"The descendant, Zhū, is enlightened."
The Emperor said: "Alas! He is obstinate and quarrelsome,
is he suitable?"
The Emperor said:
"Who can I consult about my affairs?"
Huāndōu said:
"Ah! Gònggōng is broadly gathering people to accomplish great works."
The Emperor said:
"Alas! He speaks peacefully but acts contrary,
his appearance is respectful but his arrogance reaches the heavens."
The Emperor said:
"Ah! You, leaders of the Four Mountains,
the rushing flood is dividing the land,
The swelling waters embraced the hills and submerged the heights,
vast and boundless reaching to the sky.
The people below sighed.
"Who is able to regulate them?"
All said:
"Ah! It is Gǔn!"
The Emperor said:
"Alas! Unsuitable! He defies orders
and ruins his clan."
Yuè said:
"He is different.
Try him, and then it will be settled."
The Emperor said:
"Go, be respectful!"
For nine years,
his work was not successful.
The Emperor said:
"Ah! Four Peaks.
I have been on the throne for seventy years;
if you are able to carry out my commands,
yield my position."
Yuè said: "My insufficient virtue would disgrace the imperial throne."
He said:
"Clearly promote those in humble positions."
The Emperor said:
"Clearly promote those in humble positions."
The Chief said to the Emperor:
"There is an unmarried man below,
Spoke of Yú Shùn.
The Emperor said:
"Yes! I have heard of him.
How is he?"
Yuè said:
"The son of a blind man;
his father is stubborn,
his mother quarrelsome,
and Xiàng arrogant.
He is able to harmonize
through filial piety, and is ever diligent in governing,
not allowing wickedness."
The Emperor said:
"I will try him!"
He married his two daughters to him at this time,
and observed his conduct towards the two daughters.
He carefully sent his two daughters to the banks of the Guī River,
to be wives of Yú.
The Emperor said:
"Reverently obey!"
*Shùn Diǎn*
Yú Shùn was of humble origin.
Yáo heard of his intelligence.
He intended to have him succeed to the throne.
He tested him with various difficulties.
Thus, he composed the *Shùn Diǎn*.
It is said that examining the ancients, Emperor Shùn,
was called Chóng Huá, and he was in harmony with the Emperor.
He was deeply intelligent and enlightened,
gentle, respectful, sincere, and trustworthy.
His profound virtue ascended and became known,
so he was appointed to a position.
He carefully cultivated the Five Constant Virtues,
and the Five Constant Virtues were successfully followed.
He was admitted to oversee the Hundred Offices,
and the Hundred Offices were managed in an orderly fashion.
He was presented at the Four Gates,
and the Four Gates were in solemn harmony.
He was admitted into the great forests,
and he did not get lost in violent winds, thunder, and rain.
The Emperor said:
"Come, you, Shùn!
Inquire into affairs, examine words;
your words can fundamentally achieve results,
for three years;
you shall ascend to the Emperor's throne."
Shùn yielded due to his [lack of] virtue
and did not succeed [immediately].
On the first day of the first month,
he received the abdication at the Temple of the Accomplished Ancestor.
He examined the spinning sphere and jade sighting-tube,
in order to regulate the Seven Directors [of the heavens].
He then performed the *lèi* sacrifice to the High God,
and the *yīn* sacrifice to the Six Honored Ones,
He looked towards the mountains and rivers,
extending his reverence to all the gods.
He collected the five emblems of rank.
After a month of choosing auspicious days,
he received in audience the Sì Yuè (四岳, Four Peaks) and all the regional governors,
and distributed the emblems of rank to all the feudal lords.
In the second month of the year,
he made an eastern inspection tour,
arriving at Mount Dài Zōng (岱宗),
where he performed the Chái (柴) sacrifice.
He performed the proper sacrifices to the mountains and rivers.
He then granted an audience to the eastern feudal lords.
He harmonized the seasons and months, and rectified the calendar;
he standardized the musical pitch pipes, measurements of length, volume, and weight.
He regulated the five rites,
the five kinds of jade,
the three kinds of silk,
the two kinds of live animals,
and the one kind of dead animal
offered as gifts,
corresponding to the five ranks of vessels,
and then everything was restored.
In the fifth month,
he made a southern inspection tour,
arriving at the Nán Yuè (南岳, Southern Peak),
where he performed the rites as at Mount Dài.
In the eighth month,
he made a western inspection tour,
As for the Xī Yuè (西岳, Western Great Mountain),
everything was as before.
In the eleventh month,
on the first day, he began his inspection tour,
and arrived at Běi Yuè (北岳, Northern Great Mountain),
performing the ceremonies as he had at the western mountain.
Upon returning,
he reported his accomplishments to the Artful Ancestor (Yì Zǔ, 藝祖),
using special rites.
Every five years he made an inspection tour,
and the lords of the states assembled at court every four years;
they presented their reports in words,
he tested their abilities based on their merits,
and rewarded them with carriages and clothing according to their services.
He established the twelve provinces,
and enfeoffed the twelve mountains,
dredged the rivers.
He embodied these actions in laws and models.
He mitigated the application of the five punishments.
Whipping was used as official punishment,
flogging was used as educational punishment,
metal (money) was used for redemption.
For unintentional mistakes and natural disasters, he granted amnesty;
those who stubbornly persisted in treason, however, were punished.
Be reverent, be reverent,
be concerned about the use of punishments!
He exiled Gònggōng (共工) to Yōuzhōu (幽洲),
banished Huāndōu (驩兜) to Chóngshān (崇山),
He exiled the Sān Miáo 三苗 to Sānwēi 三危;
He executed Gǔn 鯀 at Yǔshān 羽山;
After punishing these four criminals, the whole world submitted.
After twenty-eight years,
the Emperor then passed away.
The people mourned as if they had lost their fathers and mothers.
For three years,
throughout the four seas, all musical instruments were silenced.
On the first day of the first month,
Shùn 舜 went to the ancestral shrine of Wénzǔ 文祖.
He consulted the Sì Yuè 四岳 (Four Peaks),
opened the four gates,
sharpened his four eyes,
and enhanced his four ears.
He consulted the twelve pastors,
saying:
"Oh, leaders!
Be mindful of the times! Cherish those afar, and be kind to those near,
cultivate virtue sincerely, and believe in the great,
but it is difficult to find the right person.
Then the barbarians will submit."
Shùn 舜 said:
"Oh! Sì Yuè 四岳.
Is there anyone who can exert effort
to continue the Emperor’s work,
reside in the hundred offices,
clearly discern and bestow favor?"
They all said:
"Bó Yǔ (伯禹) was appointed Minister of Works."
The Emperor said,
"Yes! Consult Yǔ (禹).
You shall regulate the waters and the land,
only then will there be great effort!"
Yǔ (禹) bowed and kowtowed,
deferring to Jì (稷), Qì (契), and Gāo Yáo (皋陶).
The Emperor said,
"Yes!
You go!"
The Emperor said,
"Qì (棄)! The common people are troubled by hunger.
You, Hòu Jì (后稷),
are to sow the various grains in season."
The Emperor said,
"Qì (契)! The people are not harmonious,
and the five relationships are not deferential.
You shall be Minister of Education,
respectfully spreading the five teachings,
with leniency."
The Emperor said,
"Gāo Yáo (皋陶)! The barbarians disturb China,
and there are robbers, thieves, and traitors.
You shall be Minister of Justice;
the five punishments shall be applied with propriety,
the five submissions shall be fairly determined,
and the five exiles shall have dwelling places,
where they shall reside for three periods.
Only the intelligent are truly trustworthy."
The Emperor said,
"Who can manage my works?"
All said,
"Chuí!"
The Emperor said,
"Excellent! Ah, Chuí,
you shall be the Gonggong (Minister of Works)."
Chuí bowed his head to the ground,
deferring to Shū, Qiāng, and Jì Bóyǔ.
The Emperor said,
"Excellent! Go then,
you are the one suited."
The Emperor said,
"Who can manage for me the upper and lower creatures, plants, trees, birds, and beasts?"
All said,
"Yì!"
The Emperor said,
"Excellent! Ah, Yì,
you shall be my Yú (Forester)."
Yì bowed his head to the ground,
deferring to Zhū, Hǔ, Xióng, and Pí.
The Emperor said,
"Excellent! Go then, you are the one suited."
The Emperor said,
"Ah, Sì Yuè (Chief of the Four Mountains),
who can oversee my three rites?"
All said,
"Bó Yí."
The Emperor said,
"Yes! Ah, Bó!
You shall be the Director of Religious Ceremonies.
Be diligent and respectful day and night,
Upright, indeed, and pure."
Bó bowed his head and prostrated himself,
And yielded (the position) to Kuí and Lóng.
The Emperor said,
"Yes. Go, be respectful!"
The Emperor said,
"Kuí!
I appoint you to direct the music,
And teach the young nobles.
Be upright yet gentle,
Generous yet respectful,
Firm yet not cruel,
Simple yet not arrogant.
Poetry expresses the intent,
Song prolongs the expression,
Sound relies on the prolongation,
Pitch harmonizes the sound.
When the eight tones are perfectly in harmony,
Without disrupting the proper order,
Gods and men will be at peace."
Kuí said,
"Oh! When I strike the stone and beat the stone,
All the beasts lead the dance."
The Emperor said:
"Lóng! I am weary of slanderous words and destructive actions,
which have disturbed my teachers.
I appoint you as Nàyán (納言, a high official in charge of delivering the emperor's orders),
issuing and receiving my commands day and night,
ensuring they are just."
The Emperor said:
"Ah! You thirty-two individuals,
be respectful! Diligently illuminate the tasks of Heaven."
For three years, assess performance;
After three assessments,
promote or demote, the hidden and the manifest,
all meritorious achievements will be illustrious.
Divide the Sān Miáo (三苗, an ancient tribe) to the north.
Shùn lived to thirty, was employed
for thirty, and reigned
for fifty years, then ascended to Heaven and died.
The Emperor regulated the lower lands,
establishing residences in different regions,
differentiating births and classifying people,
creating the "Gǔ Zuò (汩作)" and
"Jiǔ Gòng (九共)" in nine chapters.
"Gǎo Yù (槀飫)".
The "Dà Yǔ Mó (大禹謨)".
Gāo Yáo (皋陶) declared his plans,
Yǔ (禹) accomplished his work,
Dì Shùn expanded upon them.
He composed the "Dà Yǔ," "Gāo Yáo Mó," and
"Yì Jì."
"Examining antiquity,"
Dà Yǔ said, "Wén Mìng's
influence spread to the four seas,
respectfully receiving (mandates) from the Emperor."
It said,
"If the ruler can overcome difficulties in being a ruler,
and the ministers can overcome difficulties in being ministers,
then the government will be well-ordered,
and the common people will be diligent in virtue."
The Emperor said,
"Excellent!
If it's truly like this,
then good words will not be suppressed.
The countryside will have no neglected talents,
and 'all states will be at peace.'"
Consider the masses.
"Abandon self and follow others,"
"Do not mistreat those with no one to appeal to,
and do not abandon the poor and distressed."
Only the Emperor can accomplish this.
Yì said,
"Ah!
"The Emperor's virtue spreads widely,
he is both sage and divine,
both martial and cultured."
Huáng Tiān bestows its favor and mandate,
encompassing all within the four seas, to be ruler of the world.
Yǔ said:
"Following goodness brings good fortune,
while going against it leads to calamity—
like echoes following sounds."
Yì said:
"Ah!
Be cautious!
Be vigilant in times of peace,
not losing sight of the laws and standards,
not indulging in idleness,
not being excessive in pleasure."
"Appoint the worthy without hesitation,
remove the wicked without doubt."
Doubtful plans should not be carried out;
may all intentions be grand and bright.
Do not violate the Way to seek the praise of the people,
and do not go against the people to indulge your own desires.
Be neither negligent nor dissolute,
and the barbarians of the four directions will come to pay tribute.
Yǔ said:
"Oh!
May the Emperor keep this in mind!
Virtue lies in good governance,
and governance lies in nurturing the people.
Water, fire, metal, wood, earth, and grain
should be well managed;
"Correcting virtue, utilizing resources, and enriching the people,
prioritize harmony."
"The nine accomplishments should be related,
and these narrations ought to be sung in songs."
"Punish them with leniency,
control them with awe,
persuade them with the nine songs,
that they not become corrupt."
The Emperor said:
"Yes!
"Earth is leveled and Heaven is complete."
"The six treasuries and three affairs are truly well-governed;
the myriad generations will forever depend on it;
this is your achievement."
The Emperor said:
"Come
you, Yǔ!
I have occupied the imperial throne for thirty-three years;
in my old age, I am weary of diligence.
Only you are not lazy;
oversee my officers."
Yǔ said:
"My virtue is insufficient,
and the people do not rely on me.
"Gāoyáo assiduously cultivates virtue;
and virtue will descend."
"The common people cherish him."
May Your Majesty consider this.
"[Niàn zī zài zī,"
"Shì zī zài zī,"
"Míng yán zī zài zī,"
"Yǔn chū zī zài zī."
"Wéi Dì niàn gōng."]
The Emperor said,
"Gāo Yáo!
'Only these are my subjects.'
None dare to correct me.
'You be the Judge.'
Be clear on the five punishments
to assist the five teachings.
Aim at my governance
so that punishment aims at no punishment,
and the people are harmonious in the mean.
Then this will be your merit. Great indeed!"
Gāo Yáo said,
"The Emperor's virtue has no fault.
In approaching those below, he is simple;
in governing the masses, he is lenient.
Punishment does not extend to descendants;
rewards extend to generations.
'Forgive faults, no matter how great;
punish offenses, no matter how small.'
When in doubt about a crime, err on the side of lightness;
when in doubt about merit, err on the side of heaviness.
'Rather than kill the innocent,
it is better to err against principle.'
The virtue of cherishing life
resonates thoroughly with the people's hearts.
Hereby, [I] will not trespass against the authorities.
The Emperor said:
"Let me follow my desires to govern."
The winds stir in all directions;
this is all due to your excellence.
The Emperor said:
"Come!
Yǔ."
"[You] sent down water as a warning to me."
"[You] have truly achieved success."
Only you are virtuous,
diligent in service to the state,
and frugal in managing your household,
not complacent or conceited.
Only you are virtuous.
"Because you do not boast,
no one in the world can compete with you in ability."
Because you do not brag,
no one in the world can compete with you in merit.
I esteem your virtue,
and praise your great achievements.
"The mandate of Heaven now rests on your person."
You shall ultimately ascend to become the great sovereign.
"The human heart is precarious,
the heart of the Dao is subtle."
Be refined and unified;
"Sincerely hold to the middle way."
Do not listen to unsubstantiated words;
Do not employ plans that have not been consulted upon.
Whom should one love if not the ruler?
Whom should one fear if not the people?
"If the multitude did not have a principal ruler (yuán hòu),
whom would they support?
If the ruler did not have the multitude,
there would be no one to guard the state."
Be respectful!
"Be careful in your position."
Reverently cultivate what is desirable.
"When the four seas are in distress and poverty,
the heavenly mandate will come to an end."
"Only from the mouth do good and war arise."
My words will not be repeated.
Yǔ said:
"Examine and divine the meritorious ministers;
only follow what is auspicious."
The Emperor said:
"Yǔ!
In divination regarding appointments, first conceal your own will,
and then consult fate through the great tortoise shell.
My will is already determined,
consultation and planning are all in agreement,
the spirits will depend on it,
the tortoise and milfoil will both comply.
'Divination does not repeat what is auspicious.'"
Yǔ bowed his head and
firmly declined.
The Emperor said,
"Do not!
Only you are suitable."
On the first day of the first month,
he received the mandate at the divine ancestral temple;
leading the hundred officials, as if it were the Emperor's first reign.
The Emperor said,
"Ah,
Yǔ!
Because the Miáo tribe are disobedient,
you shall go and punish them!"
Thereupon Yǔ assembled the feudal lords,
and made a declaration to his army, saying:
"O ye numerous officers,
listen all to my commands.
Those stupid Miáo,"
are benighted and disrespectful,
arrogant and self-important,
opposing the Way and ruining virtue.
"The superior man is in obscurity,
the inferior man is in office."
The people are abandoned and unprotected;
Heaven sends down calamity.
Therefore, I, with you, the multitude of officers,
"Obeying the words, punish the crime!"
May you all unite your hearts and strength,
They were able to achieve meritorious deeds.
For three ten-day periods,
the Miáo people defied orders.
Yì praised Yǔ, saying:
"Only virtue moves Heaven;
no distance is beyond its reach.
Complacency invites loss,
humility receives benefit;
this is the way of Heaven."
The Emperor initially at Lìshān,
"went to the fields,
and daily wept to the sky
and to his parents."
Bearing guilt and admitting fault,
"he respectfully went to see Gǔsǒu,
reverent and trembling.
Gǔ also approved."
Sincerity to this extent moves the spirits;
how much more so these Miáo?
"Yǔ bowed and said in admiration:
Ah!"
He withdrew the troops and prepared for a triumphant return.
The Emperor then extensively spread his civilizing virtue,
and performed a dance with shields and feathers on the two staircases.
For seven ten-day periods, the Miáo submitted.
The "Gāoyáo Mó"
says, "Examining antiquity," Gāoyáo said:
“Sincerely following virtue,
planning with clarity and assisting with harmony.”
Yǔ said:
“Yes! How should we do this?”
Gāo Yáo said:
“Ah! Be careful in cultivating
yourself, think of the lasting consequences.
Treat the nine branches of your family with kindness and in order,
encourage all to be diligent and supportive,
what is near can reach far,
it lies within this.”
Yǔ bowed to the excellent words,
saying: “Yes!”
Gāo Yáo said:
“Ah! It lies in knowing people,
it lies in bringing peace to the people.”
Yǔ said:
“Alas! If all could be like this,
only the Emperor would find it difficult.
Knowing people is wisdom,
enabling one to appoint people to office;
bringing peace to the people is kindness,
the common people will cherish it.
If one is wise and kind,
why worry about Huān Dōu?
Why exile the Youmiao?
Why fear those with clever words
and insinuating appearances who are truly wicked?”
Gāo Yáo said:
"Oh! There are indeed nine virtues in conduct.
If it is said that a person possesses virtue,
then it is said:
'Carrying out the collection, the collection.'"
Yǔ said:
"What are they?"
Gāo Yáo said:
"Generous yet dignified,
gentle yet firm,
sincere yet respectful,
capable yet reverent,
yielding yet resolute,
upright yet amiable,
simple yet honest,
firm yet reliable,
strong yet righteous.
Manifesting these constantly is auspicious!
If one daily proclaims these three virtues,
diligently and clearly understands them day and night, one can manage a household.
If one daily solemnly and reverently practices these six virtues,
one can clearly govern a state.
If one harmoniously receives and widely implements
all nine virtues in all affairs,
outstanding talents will be in office,
all officials will learn from each other,
and all artisans will work according to the proper time.
Consider the five stars [wǔ xīng],
so that the various achievements may be solidified.
Do not allow unrestrained desires to prevail in the states.
Be cautious and diligent,
treat every day as if it were two days, concerning yourselves with myriad affairs.
Do not neglect the numerous officials;
when Heaven's work [tiān gōng] is done, people will take over.
Heaven's order has its rules.
Carefully order our five canons and five moral principles!
Heaven's hierarchy has its rites.
Starting with our five rites,
may they be put to use!
Together, respectfully and harmoniously,
let us be of one mind!
Heaven's mandate is virtuous,
let there be five grades of clothing and five patterns!
Heaven's punishment is for the guilty,
let there be five punishments applied accordingly!
Let political affairs be promoted! Promote them!
Heaven is intelligent,
and from our people comes intelligence;
Heaven is wisely awe-inspiring,
and from our people comes wise awe.
Communicate with those above and below,
and be respectful in the lands you possess!"
Gāo Yáo said:
"My words are beneficial,
and can be put into practice."
Yǔ said:
"Yes!
Your words can be successfully accomplished."
Gāo Yáo said:
"I do not yet have the wisdom to think this through;
I only assist in praising your actions!"
*Yì Jì*
The Emperor said:
"Come! Yǔ, you also speak clearly."
Yǔ bowed and said:
"Ah! Emperor. What can I say?
I have been thinking diligently day after day."
Gāo Yáo said:
"Alas! How so?"
Yǔ said:
"The floods spread to the heavens,
vast and wide, embracing the mountains and submerging the hills;
the common people were mired in darkness.
I traveled by the four conveyances,
following the mountains and cutting down trees.
Together with Yì, I presented the people with abundant fresh food.
I dredged the nine rivers,
guiding them to the four seas;
I deepened the ditches and canals,
channeling them into the rivers.
Together with Jì, I sowed seeds, presenting the people with abundant hard-to-obtain food and fresh food,
promoting the exchange
Whether something exists or not is where transformation resides.
The masses then have grain to eat,
and all states achieve order."
Gāoyáo said:
"Yes! Master, your words are illuminating."
Yǔ said:
"Ah! O Emperor, be careful in your position."
The Emperor said:
"Yes!"
Yǔ said:
"Settle where you should settle,
and only then will there be caution and peace;
those who assist you must be upright,
and then every move will receive a great response.
Aspire to manifest your will to receive it from the High God,
and Heaven will repeatedly decree blessings upon you."
The Emperor said:
"Alas! You are a minister and a neighbor!
A neighbor and a minister!"
Yǔ said:
"Yes!"
The Emperor said:
"Ministers act as my limbs, officers, ears, and eyes.
I wish to have the people on my left and right,
and you will assist me;
I wish to exert my strength in all directions,
and you will act;
I wish to observe the emblems of the ancients,
Sun, moon, stars,
mountains, dragons, pheasant,
sacrificial cups,
algae, fire, powdered rice,
axe, symbol 亞 (fúfú), fine linen and embroidery.
Use the five colors to display them on the five types of silk,
to make garments.
You must understand;
I want to hear the six pitch-pipes,
five notes, and eight musical instruments,
whether well-governed or neglected.
Use them to introduce and express my words,
you listen;
if I err,
you correct me;
do not agree to my face,
and then speak ill of me behind my back.
Respect the four neighboring states,
in order to keep away the deceitful,
if things are not on schedule
wait and investigate to understand why,
report this to record.
Must the writing be noted,
desiring concurrent prosperity?
The artisan should offer suggestions,
from time to time lift it up;
if acceptable, you should uphold it and use it;
if not, you should intimidate him.”
Yǔ said:
"Excellent! O Emperor.
Under the glorious heaven,
reaching to the corners of the sea,
the black-haired people,
the myriad states and the Lí people offer their tribute,
all thinking of you as their sovereign.

your ancestors and fathers,

It was not merely about the number of officials,
But about the right people.
Now I, the young son,
Am reverently diligent in virtue,
Striving day and night without respite.
Looking up to the precedents of former generations, conforming to those
instructions,
To guide their officials.
"Appoint the Grand Preceptor (Tài Shī 太師), the Grand Tutor (Tài Fù 太傅), and the Grand Guardian (Tài Bǎo 太保),
"These are the Three Dukes."
They discuss the Way and manage the state,
and harmonize yin and yang.
"Offices need not be fully staffed,
but the right person is essential."
"Shǎoshī (少師), Shǎofù (少傅), and Shǎobǎo (少保)
are called the Three Solitaries."
They assist the Dukes in spreading civilization,
respectfully aid Heaven and Earth,
and support me, the One Man (the ruler).
The Zhǒngzǎi (冢宰) is in charge of governing the state,
commands all the officials,
and harmonizes the four seas.
The Sītú (司徒) is in charge of state education,
spreads the five constant virtues,
and pacifies the myriad people.
The Zōngbó (宗伯) is in charge of state rituals,
governs spirits and men,
and harmonizes those above and below.
The Sīmǎ (司馬) is in charge of state administration,
commands the six armies,
and pacifies the country.
The Sīkòu (司寇) is in charge of state prohibitions,
investigates the treacherous and wicked,
and punishes violence and rebellion.
The Sīkōng (司空) is in charge of state land,
settles the four classes of people,
and manages the benefits of the land according to the seasons.
The Six Ministers (Liù Qīng) divided their responsibilities,
each leading their subordinates,
to guide the governors of the nine provinces (jiǔ mù),
and enrich and nurture the myriad people (zhào mín).
Every six years,
those within the Five Domains (wǔ fú) came to court once.
After another six years,
the king then made a timely tour.
He examined the institutions (zhì dù) at the Four Sacred Peaks (Sì Yuè);
the feudal lords (zhū hóu) each paid homage at their respective regional peaks (fāng yuè),
and clearly distinguished promotions and demotions (chù zhì).
The king said:
"Alas!
All of you, my officials and gentlemen,
respectfully attend to your duties,
and be careful when issuing commands.
Once a command is issued, it must be carried out;
do not allow it to be reversed.
Destroy private interests for the sake of the public good,
and the people will surely embrace you.
Study the classics before taking office;
'decide matters based on established rules',
and your governance will not be confused.
Let those who understand established norms be your teachers;
do not let glib talk disrupt your offices.
Harboring doubt ruins plans;
negligence wastes government affairs;
being unlearned is like facing a wall;
Attending to affairs is indeed troublesome.
I caution you, my ministers,
Achievement is elevated only through ambition,
accomplishment is broadened only through diligence,
only through decisive action,
will there be no future difficulties.
In position, do not expect arrogance,
in emolument, do not expect extravagance.
Respect and frugality are virtues,
"do not carry your falsehoods."
Practicing virtue,
the heart is at ease, and the days are prosperous;
Practicing deceit,
the heart is burdened, and the days are inept.
"In favor, think of danger,"
there is nothing that is not to be feared,
"not fearing leads to fearing."
Promote the worthy and yield to the capable,
then the various officials will be harmonious;
discord leads to unwieldy governance.
Appointing the capable to their offices,
this is your competence;
Commending those who are not qualified,
this is your incompetence.
The King said:
Alas!
"You three ministers and you high officials,"
respect your offices,
When there is disorder, establish governance;
thereby assist your ruler,
bring lasting peace to the myriad people,
and cause the myriad states to have no weariness [of your rule].
After Chéng Wáng had attacked the Eastern Yí,
the Sùshèn came to offer congratulations.
The king ordered Róng Bó to compose "The Charge to the Sùshèn Regarding Tribute."
The Duke of Zhōu was in Fēng,
near death.
He wished to be buried in Chéng Zhōu.
The duke died.
Chéng Wáng buried him in Bì,
and reported [this event] to the Duke of Zhōu.
[He] composed "Bó Gū."
“Jūn Chén”
After the Duke of Zhōu had died,
[the king] charged Jūn Chén to separately govern the eastern outskirts of Chéng Zhōu.
[He] composed “Jūn Chén.”
The king spoke thus:
"Jūn Chén!
It is that you possess fine virtue, filial piety, and reverence.
'You are filial and friendly toward your brothers,
and are able to implement governance.'
I charge you to govern this eastern suburb;
Be respectful!
In the past, the Dōu Gōng served as a teacher and protector of the myriad people,
and the people cherished his virtue.
Go and be careful in your duties,
thus follow his constant ways,
diligently make manifest the teachings of Dōu Gōng,
and the people will be well-governed.
I have heard it said:
Supreme governance is like fragrant incense,
moving even to the spirits.
"Millet and sorghum are not fragrant,
but bright virtue alone is fragrant."
You should follow the plans and teachings of Dōu Gōng,
be diligent day by day,
and dare not be idle or complacent.
"Ordinary people who have not seen a sage
act as if they cannot see him;
having seen a sage,
they still may not follow his example."
Be warned!
"You are the wind,
the common people are the grass."
Plan your government,
and there will be none without difficulties.
There will be things to abandon and things to establish.
"In coming and going, consult your teachers,
and when opinions on matters of state are the same, then report them."
"If you have excellent plans and strategies,
Then go inside and report to your queen,
and then you will follow her instructions outside.
Saying,
"These plans and these strategies
are solely due to the virtue of our queen."
Alas!
If all ministers and people follow this,
how excellent and manifest it will be!"
The king said,
"Jūn Chén!
You must greatly promote the grand teachings of the Duke of Zhōu,
do not rely on power to create awe,
do not lean on the law to diminish [them].
Be lenient but with regulations,
be composed and harmonious.
The people of Yīn are in exile,
if I say exile,
you must not exile;
if I say pardon,
you must not pardon;
only aim for the middle ground.
If there are those who do not conform to your administration,
who are not transformed by your teachings,
exile them to stop exile, then exile them.
Those who are entrenched in treachery and wickedness,
who ruin the norms and disrupt the customs,
must not be pardoned for even the smallest offenses.
Do not be angry or resentful towards the obstinate,
「Wú qiú bèi yú yī fū」: "Do not demand perfection from a single man."
「Bì yǒu rěn,」: "There must be forbearance,"
「qí nǎi yǒu jì.」: "then there will be accomplishment."
Yǒu róng,: "With tolerance,"
dé nǎi dà.: "virtue becomes great."
Jiǎn jué xiū,: "Simplify his cultivation,"
yì jiǎn qí huò bù xiū;: "also simplify that which he may not cultivate;"
jìn jué liáng,: "Advance his goodness,"
yǐ shuài qí huò bù liáng.: "in order to guide that which may be not good."
Wéi mín shēng hòu,: "When the people's livelihood is substantial,"
yīn wù yǒu qiān.: "it changes according to circumstances."
Wéi shàng suǒ mìng,: "Violating what superiors command,"
cóng jué yōu hǎo.: "following that which they prefer."
Ěr kè jìng diǎn zài dé,: "If you can respectfully observe the standards residing in virtue,"
shí nǎi wǎng bù biàn,: "then things will invariably change,"
yǔn shēng yú dà yóu.: "and truly ascend to the great path."
Wéi yǔ yī rén yīng shòu duō fú,: "Only I, the one man, receive much blessing,"
qí ěr zhī xiū,: "and your prosperity,"
zhōng yǒu cí yú yǒng shì.: "will ultimately have words of praise in eternity."
《Gù Mìng》: "The Gu Ming (Testamentary Charge)"
Chéng Wáng jiāng bēng,: "King Cheng was about to die,"
mìng Shào Gōng, Bì Gōng shuài zhū hóu xiāng Kāng Wáng.: "and ordered the Duke of Shao and the Duke of Bi to lead the various lords in assisting King Kang."
Zuò 《Gù Mìng》.: "This is the composition of 'The Testamentary Charge'."
Wéi sì yuè: "In the fourth month,"
zāi shēng pò,: "the moon being newly born,"
Wáng bù yì.: "the King was not at ease."
On the day Jiazi,
the King then rinsed his face with water;
he was assisted in putting on his crown and ceremonial robes,
and leaned on a jade stool.
He then together summoned Tài Bǎo Shì,
Ruì Bó, Tóng Bó, Bì Gōng,
Wèi Hóu, Máo Gōng, Shī Shì,
Hǔ Chén, the various Yin, and the Yù Shì.
The King said:
"Alas! My illness has progressed to a great extent,
and is critical.
My sickness grows daily,
and I am already near death.
I fear I will not be able to swear an oath regarding the heir,
therefore I carefully instruct and command you.
In the past, Kings Wén Wáng and Wǔ Wáng
brightly manifested their virtue, established beautiful
and clear teachings, and then practiced them.
Practicing without deviation,
they were able to attain the great Mandate of Yin.
Those ignorant ones who came after,
reverently welcomed the majesty of Heaven,
and succeeded in guarding the great teachings of Wén Wáng and Wǔ Wáng,
daring not to be confused or transgress.
Now, Heaven has sent down illness, and I am near death,
unable to recover or understand.
You should clearly understand my words at this time,
and respectfully protect the Crown Prince Zhāo,
Respectfully preserve the heir Zǐ Zhāo 子釗,
and greatly assist him in times of hardship.
Be kind to those far away and capable with those near,
pacify and encourage the small and great, all the states.
If someone thinks to create disorder
through their own imposing demeanor,
you must not let Zǐ Zhāo 子釗 presume upon such improper opportunities."
Having now received the command, he returned,
and placed the ceremonial robe in the courtyard.
The next day, Yǐ Chǒu 乙丑, the king died.
The Grand Protector ordered Zhòng Huán 仲桓 and Nángōng Máo 南宮毛,
ordering them to summon
Marquis Qí 齊, Lǚ Jí 呂伋, with two shields and spears,
and a hundred Hǔ Bēn 虎賁 guards to meet Zǐ Zhāo 子釗
outside the South Gate;
they escorted him into the side chamber to mourn at the ancestral residence.
On Dīng Mǎo 丁卯, he ordered the scribe to make records.
Seven days later, on Guǐ Yǒu 癸酉,
Báixiàng 伯相 ordered Shì Xūcái 士須材
to set up the embroidered screen and the ceremonial robe.
Facing south in the window space, they laid down layers of fine bamboo mats,
with embroidered borders,
and jade-ornamented armrests.
Facing east in the west wing,
they laid down layers of close-woven mats with embroidered borders,

Facing west in the east wing,
they laid down layers of thick mats with painted borders,
A carved jade armrest.
Facing south and slightly west,

lacquered armrest.
Yue jade in five layers: displayed treasures,

High officials and feudal lords

ascends the guest stairs,

It says:
"The Queen Mother relies on the jade armrest,
to promote these final instructions,
ordering you to inherit the teachings,
and govern the Zhōu (周) kingdom;
follow the great laws,
harmonize the world,
to repay the shining teachings of Wén (文) and Wǔ (武)."
The king bows twice,
and rises. He replies:
"I, a humble and insignificant youth,
how can I manage to govern
the four quarters
and reverently fear the majesty of Heaven?"
Then he received the tokens of authority,
The king stayed three nights, performed three sacrifices,
and thrice inquired. The
chief of the ancestral temple said: "Accept it."
The Grand Protector received the token,
descended, and washed his hands.
Using a different token, he held a jade tablet to present the wine.
He handed the token to the clan officer; bowed,
and the king returned the bow.
The Grand Protector received the token, sacrificed,
tasted, and settled.
He handed the token to the clan officer, bowed,
and the king returned the bow.
The Grand Protector descended.
Collected [the tokens].
The lords exited the temple gate and waited.
"The Announcement of King Kāng"
King Kāng had already succeeded to the position of the Son of Heaven.
Thereupon he announced to the lords.
He composed "The Announcement of King Kāng".
The king came out and was inside the Ying Gate.
The Grand Protector led the western lords
Entering to the left of the Yìng Gate,
Bì Gōng led the eastern lords
entering to the right of the Yìng Gate,
all arrayed in carriages adorned with yellow and vermilion.
The guest, presenting the jade tablet and additional gifts, said:
"We, the two ministers of Wèi,
dare to hold this territory as an offering."
All bowed twice and kowtowed.
The King, inheriting virtue, replied with
a bow.
Tài Bǎo and Ruì Bó
both stepped forward, greeted each other with cupped hands,
bowed twice and kowtowed, saying:
"We dare to respectfully inform the Son of Heaven,
that August Heaven changed the mandate of the great state of Yīn,
and only the Zhōu kings Wén and Wǔ
received the great blessing,
and were able to care for the western lands.
Now, with the new ascending King,
fully harmonize rewards and punishments,
firmly establish your achievements,
and thus spread the blessings to future generations.
May the King be reverent!
Expand and display the six armies.
Do not ruin the mandate of our late great ancestor."
The King responded, saying:
"You lords of the various states, Hóu, Diān, Nán, Wèi,
I, Zhāo, alone, make this declaration.
Formerly, when you, rulers Wén and Wǔ, greatly brought peace and prosperity,
you did not focus on finding fault.
You completely reached a state of perfect sincerity and trustworthiness,
thereby illuminating the world.
Therefore, you also had brave and fierce warriors
and ministers of undivided loyalty,
who protected and governed the royal house,
and thus received a mandate from God.
August Heaven instructed them with its ways,
entrusting them with the four quarters,
and then commanded them to establish lords and set up screens
to protect us, the descendants.
Now, I, along with my uncles,
still together carefully consider
to pacify your late grandfather's ministers and bring them to serve the former king.
Although you are physically outside the court,
your hearts are surely always in the royal house.
Therefore, pay attention to and show compassion,
do not bring shame to your orphaned children."
The assembled dukes all listened to the command,
greeted each other, hurried out,
the king took off his crown and returned to mourning clothes.
*Bì Mìng* (The Charge to Bì)
King Kāng ordered the scribe Bì
to divide and settle the neighborhoods
in the suburbs of Chéngzhōu.
He composed the *Bì Mìng*.
"It was the twelfth year,
the sixth month, *gēngwǔ* (庚午) at the first quarter of the moon."
Three days later, on *rénshēn* (壬申),
"the King walked from Zōngzhōu (宗周)
to Fēng (豐)."
With the people of Chéngzhōu (成周),
he charged Duke Bì (畢公) to protect and govern the eastern suburbs.
The King spoke thus:
"Alas!
Father and Teacher!
Wén Wáng (文王) and Wǔ Wáng (武王) spread great virtue throughout the world,
thereby being able to receive the mandate of Yin (殷).
Zhōu Gōng (周公) assisted the former kings on their left and right,
'pacifying and settling their family'.
He carefully managed the obstinate people of Yin (殷),
relocating them to Luòyì (洛邑),
close to the royal palace,
to be transformed by his teachings.
Now having passed three cycles of twelve years,
the world has changed and customs have shifted,
the four quarters are without worries,
and I, the One Man, am at peace.
The Way has its ups and downs,
governance changes with the times,
if good is not praised,
the people will have nothing to strive for.
You, Sir, have cultivated virtue,
and been diligent in small matters,
assisting and enlightening the four generations,
upright in appearance and leading those below,
none failing to revere and follow your words.
Your meritorious achievements surpass those of the former kings,
allowing me, the small one, to achieve completion through passive respect.
The King said:
Alas!
Father and Teacher!
Now I respectfully entrust you with the affairs of the Duke of Zhōu.
Go!
"Distinguish clearly between the good and the wicked,
and mark their dwellings."
"Promote the good and punish the evil,"
"establish their reputation."
Those who do not follow the teachings,
alter their land boundaries,
so that they may learn to fear and admire.
Clearly delineate the boundaries of the suburbs,
carefully secure the defenses of the borders,
in order to bring peace to the four seas.
Governance values consistency,
and words should emphasize the essential,
do not just pursue novelty.
The customs of Shāng are decadent,
valuing eloquent speakers as wise,
and the remnants of this influence have not yet disappeared.
May you, my lord, give this thought!
I have heard it said:
Families with hereditary stipends
Rarely conform to ritual propriety.
To indulge in dissipation and violate virtue
Truly goes against the Way of Heaven.
Abandon simplicity and embrace extravagance,
And for myriad generations, the same trend will continue.
These Yin commoners,
Entrenched in their pampered ways, clinging only to the old,
Relying on extravagance to extinguish righteousness,
Wearing finer clothes than their superiors.
Arrogant, licentious, boastful, and extravagant,
They will surely meet with an evil end.
Even if you try to rein in their minds,
It will be extremely difficult to restrain them.
If wealth can be used to teach,
Then "it will lead to lasting years."
Only virtue and only righteousness
Are then the great teaching.
If you do not follow the ancient teachings,
What other teachings will you follow?
The King said:
Alas!
Grand Tutor!
The security or danger of the state
Depends solely on these Yin officers.
"Neither too stern nor too yielding,"
His virtue was truly cultivated.
Only the Duke of Zhōu 周公 was able to be careful at the beginning,
Only Jūn Chén 君陳 was able to harmonize in the middle,
Only Gōng 恭 was able to bring it to a successful conclusion.
The three rulers cooperated in their hearts,
And together reached the Dao.
The Dao permeated governance,
"And its beneficence nourished the people."
The four barbarian tribes with their robes fastened on the left
None did not rely on them.
I, the small child, will forever receive much blessing.
May you, my lord, at this time, complete Zhōu 周
And establish an unending foundation,
And also have unending fame.
May your descendants follow his completed model,
And govern well.
Alas!
Do not say that you are unable,
But only set your heart on it;
Do not say that the people are few,
But only be careful in your affairs.
Respectfully follow the accomplished achievements of the former kings,
And find good in their previous policies.
*Jūn Yá 君牙*
King Mù of Zhōu 周穆王 appointed Jūn Yá 君牙
To be the Grand Minister of Instruction of Zhōu 周.
He composed the *Jūn Yá 君牙*.
The King said:
"Alas!
Jūn Yá!
Your ancestors and fathers
for generations were sincerely loyal,
serving the royal house,
and they achieved great accomplishments,
which were recorded in the Tàicháng.
I, the young one, inherit and guard the legacy of King Wén, King Wǔ, King Chéng, and King Kāng;
and rely on the ministers of the former kings
to be able to govern and bring order to the four quarters.
The anxiety and peril in my heart
are like treading on a tiger's tail,
or crossing over spring ice.
Now I appoint you to be my wing,
to act as my limbs and heart.
Continue your former service,
and do not disgrace your ancestors.
Widely spread the Five Constant Virtues,
and thereby harmonize the people's rules.
If your person can be upright,
none will dare not be upright.
If the people's hearts are not centered,
you must be their center.
'When the summer is hot and rainy,
the common people only complain and sigh;
when the winter is severely cold,
The common people only say, "We resent and complain."
How truly difficult it is!
Ponder the difficulty in order to plan for ease,
and the people will then find peace.
Alas!
"How grand and evident
are the plans of Wén Wáng!
How greatly inherited
are the achievements of Wǔ Wáng!
They enlighten and assist us, their descendants,
so that all act correctly without fault."
If you reverently understand these instructions,
then you will conform to the ways of the former kings.
"Proclaim and extol the bright mandate of Wén and Wǔ,"
and emulate your predecessors.
The king spoke, saying:
Jūnyá!
It is through the old standards and models of the former upright ministers
that the order or disorder of the people lies.
Follow the conduct of your ancestors,
and illuminate the good governance of your prince.
"The Jiǒng Mandate"
King Mù commanded Bó Jiǒng
to be the Zhōu Grand Charioteer.
He composed "The Jiǒng Mandate."
The king spoke, saying:
Bo Jiong!
I am truly incapable in virtue,
inheriting the great position of my ancestors.
Apprehensive and fearful to the utmost,
I rise in the middle of the night,
thinking how to avoid their errors.
Formerly, Wén and Wǔ were intelligent and perfectly sage.
Ministers, small and great,
all cherished loyalty and goodness.
Their attendants and servants,
were without exception upright men.
Morning and evening they assisted their sovereign,
in going out, entering, rising, and resting,
there was nothing they did not treat with reverence.
In issuing proclamations and commands,
there was nothing that was not good.
The lower people reverently obeyed,
and all states enjoyed peace.
"Only I, the one man, am not good,"
truly relying on the worthy men to my left and right, front and rear,
to correct my shortcomings,
to rectify my errors and faults,
to set right my wayward thoughts,
so that I may be able to follow the example of the former worthies.
Now I appoint you to be the *Dàzhèng*,
to rectify the various servants and attendants.
Diligently cultivate your sovereign's virtue,
together repairing deficiencies.
Carefully select your colleagues,
do not use clever words and ingratiating looks,
flattering and fawning,
but only the good men.
If the servants are upright,
then the sovereign can be upright;
if the servants are flattering,
then the sovereign will consider himself a sage.
The sovereign's virtue depends on his ministers,
the sovereign's lack of virtue also depends on his ministers.
Do not be intimate with base men,
who fill the offices of ears and eyes,
and lead the sovereign with principles not of the former kings.
If it is not the right man who is considered good,
but only wealth that is considered good,
at that time, "neglecting their duties,"
then you will greatly fail to revere your ruler,
and I will condemn you.
The King said:
"Alas!
Respectful be it!
Forever assist your sovereign in upholding the constant laws."
*Lǚ Xíng* (The Punishments of Lǚ)
The decree of Lǚ, King Mù instructed on the redemption of punishments used in the Xià dynasty.
Thus was made *Lǚ Xíng*.
Concerning the decree of Lǚ.
The King, having enjoyed the kingdom for a hundred years,
being old and feeble, then devised punishments
to question the four quarters (of the land).
The King said:
"According to ancient teachings,
Chí Yóu was the first to create disorder,
extending to the common people.
There was none who did not become a robber or thief,
like owls, they sought profit in treachery and deceit,
plundering, snatching, and falsely professing piety.
The Miáo people did not use goodness,
but controlled with punishments;
thus were created the five cruel punishments,
called *fǎ* (laws).
They slaughtered the innocent.
They began to excessively use cutting off the nose (劓 *yì*), cutting off the feet (刖 *yuè*), castration (椓 *zhuó*), and tattooing the face (黥 *qíng*);
these severe punishments were all enforced,
yet no one was without fault or excuse.
The people's prosperity gradually increased,
but became muddled and chaotic.
They did not maintain faith,
and overturned oaths and covenants.
Cruel authority led to the killing of many, and
they falsely claimed innocence to those above.

Then they are like livestock to be raised.
If you treat them badly,
Then they are your enemies.
It is like facing a deep abyss,
It is like treading on thin ice.
Indeed! Indeed!
If you fail to catch a pheasant by covering it,
Then follow the wind's direction instead.
What those above say,
Those below will use.
What those below say,
Those above will use.
You must arrange them in threes and fives.
If the farmers do not produce, then food will be lacking;
If the artisans do not produce, then the tools will be lacking;
If the merchants do not produce, the three treasures will be cut off;
If the foresters (yú) do not produce, then resources will be scarce and few.
If you wish to rise, do not act rashly.
The cart in front overturns;
the cart behind takes warning.
Those who serve their lord with unorthodox methods should be punished.
Remember people's merits,
forget people's faults;
this is how a ruler should be.
When the Son of Heaven sees anomalies, he cultivates his virtue;
when the feudal lords see anomalies, they correct their administration;
when ministers and high officials see anomalies, they rectify their duties;
when scholars and commoners see anomalies, they cultivate themselves.

Dwell in peace, think of danger.
The sage has grand plans and merits;
clear signs and definite protection.
The sage acts as a model.
To ruin standards,
one indulges in ruined rituals.
Being filial, truly filial,
being fraternal towards brothers,
extend this to those in government.
If the ruler is not righteous,
he disgraces his ancestors.
How grand is the plan of King Wén (Wén Wáng)!
How greatly King Wǔ (Wǔ Wáng) carried on the achievements!
They aided and enlightened us descendants,
so that all can be upright and without fault.
Where there were those who did not think of themselves as subjects,
they campaigned in the East;
pacified their soldiers and women,
presented their baskets of black and yellow silks,
to continue the favor shown to my Zhōu kings;
they submitted as subjects to the great city of Zhōu.
There must be forbearance,
only then can there be success.
The people can be approached,
and cannot be surpassed.
Those who act before the proper time are killed without pardon;
those who fail to act in time are killed without pardon.
Virtue is accumulated even from the smallest deeds.
Bind it with a sash.
After carving and polishing,
return it to its original simplicity.
Nurturing virtue is best done by nourishing it;
eliminating harm is best done by eradicating it completely.
Eliminate evil without hesitation;
entrust the capable without doubt.
After achieving success,
one should not remain in that position for long.
Those who rely on virtue prosper;
those who rely on strength perish.
Enrich your people.
At the Tàishè (太社) altar, only pine trees are planted;
at the East Shè (東社) altar, only cypress trees are planted;
The Southern Society values the catalpa,
the Western Society values the chestnut,
the Northern Society values the pagoda tree.
An assessment is conducted every three years,
with those who are less capable being demoted in position.
Oh, you, eldest son!
(Wear) embroidered garments,
with yellow and crimson tassels.
Be careful in the beginning and respectful to the end,
so that in the end you will not be troubled.

Yáo said:
"Oh, you, Shùn!
The mandate of Heaven rests upon your person;
sincerely hold to the middle way.
If the whole world is in poverty and distress,
the Heavenly reward will end forever."
Fàng Xūn said:
"Comfort them,
bring them in,
correct them,
straighten them,
assist them,
support them,
enable them to attain it themselves,
and then go on to elevate their virtue."
Shùn went to the fields
and wailed and cried to the vast heavens.
The Emperor sent his sons,
nine sons and two daughters,
a hundred officials, cattle, sheep, granaries all prepared,
to serve Shùn in the midst of the fields.
His parents ordered Shùn to repair the granary,
then removed the ladder;
Gǔsǒu burned the granary.
They ordered him to dredge a well,
and when he came out, they covered him up.
Xiàng said:
"Planning to cover the sovereign
is entirely my achievement.
The cattle and sheep belong to our parents,
the granaries belong to our parents,
the shields and spears are mine,
the qín zither is mine,
the dì flute is mine,
the two elder sisters-in-law will manage my dwelling."
Xiàng went towards and entered Shùn's palace.
Shùn was on the bed playing the qín.
Xiàng said:
"I am full of yearning and longing for you, my lord!"
He felt ashamed.
Shùn said:
"With these subjects,
You should assist me in governing."
Wanting to see him frequently,
he came continuously,
and could not reach the place for tribute.
He used the administration of affairs to meet with the Yǒu Bēi people.
Yī Yǐn said:
"I will not get close to those who are not compliant."
The king said:
"Do not be afraid!
I will comfort you;
I am not an enemy of the people."
As if collapsing, he knocked his head to the ground.
Yǔ said:
"Vast is the multitude,
all listening to my words.
It is not that I, a humble person,
dare to cause chaos on my own accord;
but these stupid Yǒu Miáo,
deserve the punishment of Heaven.
If I lead all of you against all of them,
to attack Yǒu Miáo."
The approval was not obvious,
it is only that the people of Heaven are not protected.
Having guarded against evil intentions,
Heaven adds its blame.
Not being careful about their virtue,
how can Heaven's mandate be protected!
They constantly dance in the palace,
this is called shamanic wind.
As for punishment,
gentlemen contribute two *wèi* of silk,
commoners do not.
Like the paths of the two lords Huáng.
Then they said:
Alas!
The dance is unrestrained,
the boastful words are very clear.
God is not constant,
the nine regions will perish because of it.
God is not compliant,
he sends down hundreds of calamities;
their families will surely be ruined and lost.
Oh, a sage and martial leader knows people,
in order to screen and assist himself.
To establish a state and set up a capital,
and then make lords, kings, and dukes,
it is to use adversity and employ prosperity.
To make light of high officials and teachers,
is to employ adversity in times of ease.
It is through keen discernment that one is able to govern and maintain the balance of Heaven.
